title: Sewing Machine Needles Explained: Sizes, Types & Systems
description: A clear guide to sewing machine needles: domestic and industrial systems, sizes like 80/12 and 100/16, and points for jersey, denim, leather and embroidery.
intro: The cheapest part of your machine has the biggest effect on stitch quality. Here is how to choose the right needle.

image.alt: Macro photo of a sewing machine needle

cardText: Needle systems, sizes and points for every fabric.

sections.html: The system is the needle’s shape and length, and it must match your machine. Most domestic machines use 130/705H (also called 15x1 or HAx1) with a flat shank. Industrial machines use round-shank systems such as DBx1 (many lockstitch machines) or DCx27 (many overlockers). Check your manual.
Sizes are shown as metric/imperial, such as 70/10, 80/12, 90/14, 100/16. Lower numbers are finer. Use fine needles for silk and lawn, mid sizes for cotton, and heavier sizes for denim and canvas.

• Universal: everyday wovens and some knits.
  • Ballpoint / jersey: pushes between knit fibres instead of piercing them.
  • Stretch: for very elastic fabrics and swimwear.
  • Jeans / denim: sharp and strong for dense weaves.
  • Leather: a cutting point, for leather only.
  • Embroidery and metallic: larger eyes to protect delicate threads.
Change the needle every project or after several hours of sewing, and immediately if it hits a pin. A blunt needle causes skipped stitches and snagged fabric.

Needles from brands such as Groz-Beckert, Organ and SCHMETZ are stocked by specialist dealers.
